title: needs-decision: bundle-work has essentially zero byte headroom left
body:
# needs-decision: bundle-work has essentially zero byte headroom left

## Background

`audit/sync-manifest.json`'s `bundle-work` (`idd-overview-appendix` +
`idd-overview-core` + `idd-work` instructions, `limitBytes: 45,000`)
sits at **97.98% utilization** on current `main`
(`5e958adb`, 2026-09-01T21:52:44+09:00):

| File | Bytes (banner-stripped) |
| --- | --- |
| `idd-overview-appendix.instructions.md` | 7,108 |
| `idd-overview-core.instructions.md` | 15,940 |
| `idd-work.instructions.md` | 21,045 |
| **Total** | **44,093** |

(Reproduced via `stripGeneratedFromBanner` + `Buffer.byteLength`,
matching `collectContextCeilingViolations`'s own formula:
`totalBytes * 100 > limitBytes * maxUtilizationPct` fails once
`totalBytes` exceeds 44,100.)

That leaves **7 bytes** of headroom before the 98% hard-fail
(`context-ceiling-200k`'s `maxUtilizationPct: 98`) — effectively none.
`bundle-work`'s `limitBytes` (45,000) is still far below the shared
196,000-byte `maxBundleLimitBytes` ceiling, so unlike #2181's
`bundle-review` situation, a conventional `limitBytes` raise (the
mechanical fix #2091 used for six bundles, and PR #2342 used for
`bundle-review` again just today) is structurally available here — but
per this repo's established practice (#2091, #2181), the amount and
whether-to-raise-vs-trim decision is a maintainer call, not one this
session should make unilaterally against a shared policy constant
(`docs/policy-constants.md`).

**How this was discovered**: while resolving a real `main`-advancing
merge conflict on PR #2374 (issue #2332, a B1 docs caveat adding one
new sentence to `idd-work.instructions.md`), the incoming `main` commit
(PR #2372, unrelated `#2218` work) had **independently trimmed the same
"Harness-native worktree tools" paragraph** I had trimmed for my own
unrelated byte-budget funding. Both sessions converged on the same
paragraph as the only visible remaining slack in the bundle — the
strongest available evidence that ad hoc per-PR trimming is exhausted
as a strategy: any two sessions editing `bundle-work`'s files now
compete for the same handful of bytes, and a session can measure
headroom at claim time only to have another session's independent,
unrelated PR consume it before merge.

## Proposed change

No single proposed change: this is a maintainer decision among the
options below, the same pattern #2091 and #2181 used for the same
class of problem.

### Options for a maintainer to choose among

1. **Raise `bundle-work`'s `limitBytes`** (currently 45,000) to restore
   working headroom, mirroring #2091's mechanical fix and PR #2342's
   same-day precedent for `bundle-review`. `bundle-work` has ample room
   under the 196,000-byte ceiling for this.
2. **Trim existing content** in `bundle-work`'s three member files under
   the manifest's documented `exemptBundles` content-diet lifecycle
   (`docs/policy-constants.md`'s "Exemption lifecycle" section) —
   requires a maintainer (or an explicitly maintainer-scoped follow-up
   issue) to choose what substantive content to cut, since the corpus
   is deliberate, cited contract text and the easy de-duplication
   opportunities are already gone (see above).
3. **Leave `bundle-work` as-is and accept the friction**: any future PR
   touching `idd-overview-core`, `idd-overview-appendix`, or `idd-work`
   instructions risks tipping the bundle over the 98% hard-fail and
   getting blocked case-by-case, the same friction #2181 documented for
   `bundle-review`.
4. **Something else the maintainer prefers.**

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A maintainer states which option above to take (or a different
      resolution) in a comment on this issue.
- [ ] Close this issue once that decision is recorded. The chosen
      option becomes a follow-up `ready` issue scoped to the exact
      manifest/content change, mirroring how #2091 and #2181 were
      resolved — this issue itself stays decision-only.

## Impact

This currently blocks issue #2332 / PR #2374 (a B1 docs caveat adding
one sentence to `idd-work.instructions.md`) from merging without either
funding its own headroom (already attempted and consumed by the #2372
collision above) or waiting on this decision. PR #2374's merge attempt
has been held back to its pre-conflict commit rather than pushed with a
failing audit; #2332 has been unclaimed pending this decision.
